task: Missing-rate filtering + median imputation -> time-based 70/30 split -> SMOTE to ~50% positive on train -> LGBM -> report train_positive_ratio_after_smote and test_ks into output.json

data_overview.join_check: features and label are 1:1 on (time, bizcode), 0 duplicate keys, row order identical (verified upstream in data_profile.json)

groups.f0-f66: 67 numeric columns; mixture of continuous floats and low-cardinality integer codes (cardinality 3-15 for many, e.g. f63: {-1,0,1})
groups.e1-e11: 11 continuous floats in ~[0,0.95] with -1 sentinel; e8-e11 show ~23.6% sentinel rate in sample
groups.x0-x19: 20 continuous floats in ~[0,80] with -1 sentinel; x10-x19 have identical min/max to x0-x9 (likely derived/duplicated variants)

time.note: rows are NOT stored in time order (sample of 5000 heads spans all 153 days) -> must sort/split explicitly

missingness.nan_missing_rate: 0.0 for all 98 features (upstream data_profile + 5000-row head sample agree)
missingness.sentinel_negative_one: 90 of 98 features use -1 as a 'not applicable/missing' sentinel, but no feature exceeds 30% (-1) in sample (max ~0.236 for e8-e11)
missingness.implication: literal NaN-based missing-rate filter drops nothing; median imputation is a no-op on NaN but the plan still runs the step so the requirement is satisfied and auditable

assumptions: Missing rate is defined on true NaN values (pandas isna) as the task states; the -1 sentinel is recorded as a diagnostic only and is NOT used to drop features (keeps output comparable to the upstream baseline in output.json).
Time split uses the first 70% of unique sorted days (not 70% of rows) to avoid leaking future days into train; this is the split already documented in data_profile.json.
Median imputation statistics are fit on the training portion only, then applied to both parts (no test leakage).
SMOTE is applied only to the training set, never to test, and only after imputation + split.
No feature standardization is required (LGBM is tree-based); no feature selection beyond the >30% missing filter.

steps.name: load_and_validate
actions: pd.read_csv('features.csv') and pd.read_csv('label.csv')
assert len equal (49910) and (time, bizcode) 1:1 merge keeps 49910 rows; assert no duplicated keys
feature_cols = all features columns except ['time','bizcode'] -> expect 98 columns

steps.name: missing_rate_filter
actions: miss = df[feature_cols].isna().mean()
dropped = [c for c in feature_cols if miss[c] > 0.30]; kept = rest
record counts: n_columns_with_any_missing, max_missing_rate, dropped list (expected: empty, kept=98)
secondary diagnostic: rate of value == -1 per feature, saved but not used for dropping

steps.name: time_split
actions: df = df.sort_values('time', kind='mergesort')
days = sorted unique time; n_train_days = floor(0.7*153) = 107 -> train days 20230701..20231015; test days 20231016..20231130 (46 days)
is_train mask = df.time.isin(train_days) -> expect 30490 train rows / 19420 test rows

steps.name: median_impute
actions: med = df.loc[is_train, kept].median()
X = df[kept].fillna(med); assert X.isna().sum().sum() == 0 after fill
y = df['label'].astype(int)
handle residual all-NaN columns defensively (none expected): drop column if med is NaN

steps.name: smote
actions: X_tr, X_te, y_tr, y_te = time-based slices of X, y
SMOTE(sampling_strategy=1.0, random_state=42, k_neighbors=5).fit_resample(X_tr, y_tr)
train_positive_ratio_after_smote = y_res.mean() (expected 0.5); record before/after row counts (~30490 -> ~55k rows)
guard: k_neighbors must be < n_minority(2954); also drop any zero-variance columns before SMOTE if it errors

steps.name: train_lgbm
actions: LGBMClassifier(n_estimators=600, learning_rate=0.03, num_leaves=31, subsample=0.8, subsample_freq=1, colsample_bytree=0.7, min_child_samples=20, reg_lambda=1.0, random_state=42, n_jobs=-1, verbose=-1)
fit on the SMOTE-resampled training data only
predict_proba on X_te (original, unsampled test) -> p_te

steps.name: evaluate_ks
actions: KS = max |CDF_pos - CDF_neg| computed on descending score order of p_te vs y_te
also log test AUC and train KS for diagnostics (not written to output.json)

steps.name: write_output
actions: json.dump({'train_positive_ratio_after_smote': round(ratio_after, 6), 'test_ks': round(ks, 6)}, open('output.json','w'), indent=2)
also persist the missing-rate table / dropped feature list to missing_rate_report.json for traceability

validation_checks: joined rows == 49910 and no duplicated (time, bizcode)
kept feature count (98) + dropped count == 98; every kept feature has NaN missing rate <= 0.30
no NaN in X after imputation
train/test day ranges strictly non-overlapping and contiguous in sorted day order
test set is never resampled: len(X_te) == 19420
test_ks sanity range 0.05-0.60; upstream baseline value is 0.129349 - a materially different value should be explained before overwriting output.json
risks_and_notes: Heavy class imbalance (9.3% positive) plus 1.0 SMOTE ratio means ~9x replication of synthetic minority in train; test distribution stays untouched, so test KS reflects the real prior.

-1 sentinel values are widespread (90/98 features). Treating them as missing would change the feature set and the model; the plan keeps the literal NaN-based rule and only documents the sentinel rate.
x10-x19 duplicate the min/max of x0-x9 -> strong collinearity; harmless for LGBM but explains low feature importance gains; no removal is done (task does not ask for it).
Many f-columns are low-cardinality integer codes; keeping them numeric (ordinal) rather than categorical is acceptable for LGBM and keeps SMOTE simple (SMOTE requires numeric input).

SMOTE interpolation on one-hot/unbalanced low-cardinality columns can create non-integer intermediate values; acceptable for this pipeline since trees are invariant to monotone transforms and no inverse mapping is needed.
Runtime: 55k x 98 matrix with 600 trees runs in well under 120s; if it is tight, split into save-to-parquet + train steps.
